messages:
incident-bot: Pager: inference-host-backpressure detected in az1a (fleet=g5-ephemeral). Alert: 502 spike + p95 token latency up 3.1s. See metrics: https://ops/alerts/3099994321 :mega:

jamie_sre: noticing connection resets from 3 instances in az1a, packet retransmits up, ephemerals hitting tx queue backpressure. 502s correlate with instance tx-sched latency.

marta_oncall: on it — taking lead. tagging @ben_srelead for handoff if this needs escalation.

jamie_sre: started quick health checks: `curl -v http://10.0.12.45:8080/health` -> intermittent `502` and long TCP handshake. Logs show `kvcache write stall` on those hosts.

ben_srelead: recommend immediate partial traffic shift off az1a, can we steer 30% to eu1b and 10% to usw2? Need capacity check.

infra-bot: Capacity query: az1a spare capacity for g5: 0.33x, eu1b spare: 1.8x, usw2 spare: 0.9x.

marta_oncall: starting rolling drain of affected ephemeral host group `g5-az1a-ephemeral-02` (grace=20s). Will enable model fallback to quantized variant for latency-sensitive routes.

deploy-bot: Traffic policy update queued: route-inference -> weight(az1a:60, eu1b:30, usw2:10). Applying now.

oliver_pm: customer impact? any apps reporting errors?

anya_support: Support logs: two customer-facing services report elevated errors (~3%) and increased latency for streaming responses. Tier-1 customers getting timeout retries. Flagging high touch customers: AcmeCorp, NimbusAI.

jamie_sre: mitigations in flight: 1) drain problematic hosts 2) shift traffic weights 3) enable prefix KV caching on fallback route 4) lower batch size for streaming.

marta_oncall: confirmed route weights updated, monitoring for request success rate. Rolling drain completed for 4 hosts; they show healthy on reboot but still higher io-wait on one host. Marked that host for reprovision.

ben_srelead: Suggest proactive alert to customers: short degradation, no request data lost, automatic reroute in progress. @anya_support can you draft a note?

anya_support: Drafting now: "We observed increased latency and transient 502s for inference in AZ1a. Traffic was shifted to other regions and full capacity restored for most customers. We continue to monitor and will provide a post-incident summary." Will ping legal for wording.

jamie_sre: Telemetry: error rate back to baseline for most routes (~0.4%). p95 latency on routed hosts down to 1.1s. Some tail errors remain on legacy small-instances behind the old NLB config.

marta_oncall: handing off to @ben_srelead for post-incident and follow-up runbook tasks. I'll stay on standby for any regressions.

ben_srelead: Acknowledged take. Next steps: 1) reprovision one problematic host (id=i-0abcde12345) 2) run IO stress test and check kernel tx-sched settings 3) adjust autoscaler for ephemeral pools to maintain higher headroom 4) schedule a short postmortem sync.

oliver_pm: Please include the cost/latency tradeoffs of quantized fallback in postmortem — product needs to know impact.

marta_oncall: setting severity P1 -> P2 (customer impact narrowed, automated reroute successful).

ben_srelead: creating post-incident ticket INF-2026-043 and assigning to eng-infra and runtime teams.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=P2, owners=[ben_srelead, eng-infra], ticket=INF-2026-043.

anya_support: Notified affected customers. Will follow up once postmortem draft is ready.

jamie_sre: leaving a short note for runbook: if az1a host tx-sched >200ms, enable immediate traffic weight shift and reprovision host; prefer larger instance types for ephemeral pool if observed sustained backpressure.

ben_srelead: thanks team — closing on-call handoff. Will run the postmortem and share timeline + actionable items. :thumbsup:
